item.title: A Thousand Prophets, a Thousand and One Sages | Rambam's Intro to the Mishnah, Part 2
item.description:
Does a prophet have any special authority to interpret the Torah? For the Rambam, none beyond any other Sage, so a thousand and one Sages outvote a thousand prophets. Also how a prophet is tested, which prophets are false, and the one-off suspension of a misvah a verified prophet may order.

item.title: Why Do the Sages Argue? The Five Categories of Torah Law | Rambam's Intro to the Mishnah, Part 3
item.description:
If the Oral Torah came from Sinai, why do the Sages argue? The Rambam's five categories of Torah law, received laws that are never disputed, Halacha LeMoshe MiSinai, why disputes multiplied as the skill of derivation weakened, and why the Mishnah records minority views.

item.title: Why Is Avot in the Order of Damages? | Rambam's Intro to the Mishnah, Part 5
item.description:
What does a tractate of ethics have to do with courts and judges? Avot's chain from Sinai grounds the authority of each generation's court, and judges need its ethics above all. Then the Rambam's account of the orders of Kodashim and Taharot, the count of tractates and chapters, and what the Talmud contains.

item.title: The Secrets Behind the Stories: Aggadah Explained | Rambam's Intro to the Mishnah, Part 6
item.description:
Why do so many of the Sages' stories look far-fetched? The Rambam's case for studying aggadah rather than skipping it: deep wisdom is wrapped in stories to invite interpretation, to guard secrets and to reach the masses, and an apparent absurdity calls for more study, not mockery.

item.title: Why Was the World Created? The Purpose of Man | Rambam's Intro to the Mishnah, Part 7
item.description:
What is the purpose of creation? The Rambam argues that everything on earth exists for the human, whose purpose is grasping truth and knowing HaShem's unity; this demands priorities rather than asceticism, and the goal is a person both wise and good.

item.title: Who Was the World Made For? Sages and the People of the Land | Rambam's Intro to the Mishnah, Part 8
item.description:
If the world exists for the rare perfected person, why are there so many others? The Rambam's two answers: the many provide for the wise and give them a society. Am haares means those who settle the land, not a slur, and greatness is chosen, not gifted.

item.title: The Whole Torah in One Book: The Rambam's Introduction to the Mishneh Torah
item.description:
Why does the Mishneh Torah need no sources? The Rambam's introduction traces forty generations from Moshe to Rav Ashi, explains why Rebbi wrote the Mishnah, why the Talmud binds all Israel and nothing later does, and what the Mishneh Torah was meant to be: a summary, not a replacement for study.
